quote: if the treatment occurred at the beginning of a recession much larger than anything seen in the pre-treatment period, then a violation of parallel trends of that magnitude may indeed be plausible

title: Few treated clusters break standard cluster-robust inference
guidance: Clustered standard errors rely on a central limit theorem across many treated and untreated clusters; with only a handful of treated states, cluster-level shocks do not average out even when each cluster has many units. Alternatives (Donald and Lang, Conley and Taber, Ferman and Pinto, Hagemann, cluster wild bootstrap) each impose restrictions on error distributions or treatment effect homogeneity that can fail with two-way fixed effects and heterogeneous effects.
action: Count the number of treated clusters in each mapped study and flag inference based on conventional clustered standard errors when that number is small.
quote: The central limit theorem may provide a poor approximation with few clusters, even if the number of units within each cluster is large.

title: Cluster at the level at which treatment is independently assigned
guidance: From a design-based perspective that treats units as fixed and treatment assignment as stochastic, cluster-robust standard errors are valid (if conservative) when clustering follows the level at which treatment is independently determined, for example the state when policy is set by states. This gives a clearer rule than the model-based advice to cluster where errors are correlated, and shows that inference remains sensible even without a conceivable super-population.
action: Check that the clustering level in each study matches the level of treatment assignment, and flag studies that cluster at a finer level.
quote: cluster-robust standard errors are valid (but potentially conservative) if the clustering is done at the level at which treatment is independently determined

title: Regression discontinuity requires a known, verifiable assignment rule
guidance: What sets regression discontinuity apart from other observational designs is that the score, cutoff and treatment rule must exist ex ante and be known and verifiable, not merely postulated by the researcher. This objective basis is what makes design-specific validation and falsification tests possible and gives the design its superior credibility among non-experimental methods.
action: When mapping a regression discontinuity study, verify that the paper documents an institutional rule linking a pre-existing score to a cutoff, rather than a threshold chosen by the authors.
quote: the score, cutoff, and treatment assignment rule must exist ex-ante and be well defined, with a discontinuous probability of treatment assignment at the cutoff. Importantly, the treatment assignment rule is known and verifiable

title: Continuity framework: two identifying assumptions at the cutoff
guidance: In the continuity framework, the sharp regression discontinuity effect is identified if the conditional expectations of both potential outcomes are continuous in the score at the cutoff and the score density is positive there. The effect is then the vertical gap between the limits of observed outcomes from each side, and it applies only to units with scores at the cutoff.
action: Record for each regression discontinuity study whether its argument for identification is continuity of potential outcome regressions at the cutoff, and what could make them jump (for example, other policies at the same threshold).
quote: the two key identifying assumptions are that (a) the regression functions E[Yi (0)|Xi = x] and E[Yi (1)|Xi = x] are continuous in x at c, and (b) the density of the score near the cutoff is positive

title: Local randomization requires an explicit exclusion restriction on the score
guidance: The alternative local randomization framework treats units in a window around the cutoff as if randomly assigned, which needs two conditions: the score's assignment mechanism in the window is known, and potential outcomes do not depend on the score within the window. Unlike a true experiment, the score in a regression discontinuity design is often correlated with potential outcomes, so this second condition must be stated and defended explicitly.
action: Where a study interprets its regression discontinuity as a local experiment, check that it argues the score has no independent effect on outcomes within the chosen window.
quote: in an RD design, the score is often correlated with the potential outcomes, and there are multiple channels by which a change in the score, even if small, might induce a change in the potential outcomes

title: Covariates cannot restore identification in regression discontinuity
guidance: As in randomised experiments, adding pre-intervention covariates cannot recover nonparametric identification of the regression discontinuity parameter if the design assumptions fail; without strong further assumptions, covariate adjustment only improves precision. Covariates should be added in ways that leave the target parameter unchanged.
action: Treat covariate adjustment in a regression discontinuity study as a precision device, and do not credit it as fixing a design with evidence of manipulation or imbalance.
quote: it is not possible to restore the nonparametric identification of canonical parameters of interest using covariate adjustment without additional strong assumptions

title: Fuzzy designs need monotonicity and exclusion, as in instrumental variables
guidance: When compliance with the cutoff is imperfect, the ratio of outcome jump to treatment-take-up jump identifies an average effect only for compliers at the cutoff, and only under a monotonicity condition and an exclusion restriction that crossing the cutoff affects the outcome solely through treatment received. Mere notification of assignment changing behaviour violates this; the intention-to-treat effect of assignment remains identified under sharp assumptions.
action: For fuzzy regression discontinuity studies, record whether the paper reports the intention-to-treat jump separately and argues monotonicity and exclusion for the complier effect.
quote: the interpretation of τ FRD as the average effect of the treatment requires that the only effect of crossing the cutoff on the outcome occur via the treatment received

title: Regression discontinuity effects are local and have low external validity
guidance: The design credibly identifies effects only at or near the cutoff; without extra assumptions nothing can be learned about effects for units with scores far from the threshold. Extrapolation methods exist but each adds assumptions such as conditional ignorability, pre-intervention outcome measures, or homogeneity across cutoffs.
action: When aggregating a field's regression discontinuity findings, note the subpopulation at the cutoff and flag any extrapolated claim together with the extra assumption it relies on.
quote: an important limitation of RD designs is that they have low external validity. In the absence of additional assumptions, it is not possible to learn about treatment effects away from the cutoff

title: Global polynomial fits are for visualisation, not for estimation
guidance: Regression discontinuity plots combine a global polynomial fit with binned local means to show the data, but a jump in the global polynomial at the cutoff should not be read as the effect: high-order polynomials behave poorly at boundaries (Runge's phenomenon) and produce counter-intuitive weights. Experiments show that changing the plot specification alone leads readers to different conclusions.
action: Discount regression discontinuity estimates based on global polynomial regressions and look for local polynomial estimates near the cutoff.
quote: such jump should not be interpreted as the definitive RD effect, as higher-order polynomial approximations are poorly behaved at or near boundary points

title: Choose the bandwidth by a data-driven optimality criterion, not by hand
guidance: Regression discontinuity results are generally sensitive to the bandwidth, so an arbitrary choice invites specification searching. The recommendation is to use a bandwidth that is optimal for a stated criterion (mean squared error or coverage error), which makes the choice transparent, removes researcher discretion, improves replicability and reduces the scope for p-hacking.
action: Check whether each regression discontinuity study reports a data-driven bandwidth selector; treat hand-picked bandwidths as a researcher degree of freedom to vary in a multiverse.
quote: the recommendation is to always use a data-driven procedure that is optimal for a given criterion, leading to a transparent, principled, and objective choice for implementation that ultimately removes the researcher's discretion

title: Conventional confidence intervals at the optimal bandwidth undercover
guidance: Local polynomial fits are approximations with smoothing bias, and a mean-squared-error-optimal bandwidth leaves bias that conventional least squares inference ignores; a nominal 95 percent interval then covers only about 80 percent of the time. Robust bias-corrected intervals estimate and remove the bias and adjust the standard error, remaining valid at the same bandwidth used for point estimation.
action: Verify that regression discontinuity inference uses robust bias-corrected confidence intervals, and treat conventional intervals at an optimal bandwidth as overstating precision.
quote: Ignoring the misspecification bias can lead to substantial overrejection of the null hypothesis of no treatment effect

title: Discrete scores break continuity-based identification
guidance: With a discrete running variable, units share mass points and no observation lies arbitrarily close to the cutoff, so the continuity-based effect is not nonparametrically identified without extrapolation from the nearest mass point. When there are few distinct values, local randomization methods or a redefined parameter are preferable, and the effective sample size is the number of mass points, not the number of units.
action: Record the number of distinct score values in each regression discontinuity study and flag continuity-based analyses with few mass points as relying on parametric extrapolation.
quote: In the absence of a continuously distributed score, standard continuity-based RD treatment effects are not nonparametrically identifiable at the cutoff

title: Validate with predetermined covariates and placebo outcomes at the cutoff
guidance: Core regression discontinuity assumptions are untestable, but indirect evidence comes from estimating the discontinuity in pre-intervention covariates and in outcomes the treatment should not affect; a jump casts doubt on the design. Because the usual balance test only controls the error of finding imbalance when groups are similar, it may be better to test the null that distributions differ.
action: Look for covariate and placebo-outcome discontinuity tests in each regression discontinuity study and note whether the test was framed as a non-inferiority (equivalence) test.
quote: Rejecting the null hypothesis implies that the treatment and control groups are not comparable in terms of pre-treatment characteristics, thereby casting doubts on the research design.

title: Density tests detect sorting but are neither necessary nor sufficient
guidance: The McCrary density test checks whether the score density is continuous at the cutoff; a discontinuity suggests endogenous sorting or administrative manipulation. However, density continuity is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity, so passing the test does not prove the design and a binomial count test in a fixed window offers a complementary check that also works with discrete scores.
action: Record whether a density or binomial manipulation test was reported, but treat a passed test as supporting rather than establishing the absence of manipulation.
quote: While continuity of the density function of the score at the cutoff is neither necessary nor sufficient for the validity of an RD design, a discontinuous density can be heuristically associated with the idea of endogenous sorting

title: Placebo cutoffs, donut holes and bandwidth sensitivity as robustness checks
guidance: Three design-specific falsification checks are to re-estimate the effect at artificial cutoffs where no jump should appear (separately on each side to avoid contamination), to drop the observations nearest the cutoff where sorting is most likely, and to vary the bandwidth or window. Much larger bandwidths than the optimal one are not informative because of misspecification bias.
action: Use the presence of placebo-cutoff, donut-hole and bandwidth-sensitivity analyses as checklist items when coding the robustness of each regression discontinuity study.
quote: because the true cutoff is the only score value at which the probability of receiving the treatment changes discontinuously, it should also be the only score value at which the outcome changes discontinuously

title: Regression discontinuity needs a score, cutoff and non-manipulable rule
guidance: The design is defined by a score, a cutoff and a hard-threshold rule, so that the probability of treatment jumps at a known point. Causal leverage comes from units barely below the cutoff serving as counterfactuals for units barely above, which only works if units cannot perfectly determine or manipulate the exact score they receive.
action: For each regression discontinuity study, record the score, cutoff and rule, and ask whether units or administrators could have set scores precisely relative to the cutoff.
quote: If units are not able to perfectly determine or manipulate the exact value of the score that they receive, the discontinuous change in the probability of treatment assignment can be used to study the effect of the treatment

title: Local randomization is a stronger assumption than continuity
guidance: Interpreting a regression discontinuity as a local experiment requires assuming that, within a window, the score is as-if randomly assigned and has no direct effect on outcomes; these conditions are stronger than continuity of the regression functions at the cutoff. The authors therefore present local randomization as a complement or robustness check when the score is continuous, and as the natural primary approach when the score is discrete.
action: When a paper justifies its design by analogy to a randomised experiment, check whether it states and tests the stronger local randomization conditions or merely invokes the analogy.
quote: local randomization approach typically requires stronger assumptions than the continuity-based

title: Direct effects of the score near the cutoff create spurious effects
guidance: Even if placement around the cutoff were randomly shuffled, a difference in outcomes could arise if the score itself affects behaviour, for example students discouraged by narrowly failing an exam. The local randomization framework therefore requires an explicit exclusion restriction (condition LR2) that potential outcomes do not depend on the score inside the window, a condition that random assignment of the score does not guarantee.
action: Ask whether the score in each regression discontinuity study carries meaning to the units (grades, vote margins, eligibility scores) that could affect outcomes independently of the treatment.
quote: also on the assumption that the value of the score within this window is unrelated to the potential outcomes—a condition that is not guaranteed by the random assignment of the score

title: Choose the local randomization window by covariate balance, not ad hoc
guidance: An ad hoc window (for example, elections decided by half a point) lacks transparency and objectivity. The recommended procedure starts with the smallest window, tests balance of predetermined covariates, and enlarges the window until balance is rejected, choosing the largest window where balance holds in it and all nested windows; this relies on at least one covariate being related to the score outside the window but not inside.
action: Record whether the window in a local randomization analysis was chosen by a data-driven balance procedure, and treat hand-picked windows as a researcher degree of freedom.
quote: The disadvantage of an ad-hoc method is that it lacks transparency and objectivity. A preferred alternative is to use a principled data-driven procedure.

title: Balance tests for window selection should use a high significance level
guidance: Because the main risk in window selection is failing to reject a false balance hypothesis, the usual 0.05 threshold is too lenient; the authors recommend rejecting balance at alpha of at least 0.15 and ideally no smaller than 0.10, using Fisherian tests, covariates related to both outcome and treatment, and at least roughly ten observations on each side of the cutoff in the smallest window.
action: When evaluating a local randomization regression discontinuity study, check the alpha level and minimum sample used in its window selection and discount windows selected with a conventional 0.05 threshold.
quote: Because the main concern is failing to reject a false H0 , the threshold significance level that determines when H0 is rejected should be higher than the usual 0.05.

title: Select the window before looking at outcome results
guidance: Separating window selection (which never shows outcome results) from effect estimation reduces the possibility of choosing the window in which the outcome points in the expected direction. Choosing the analysis window without seeing outcomes minimises pre-testing and specification searching, a principle that generalises to bandwidth and specification choices in any design.
action: Treat any regression discontinuity analysis in which the window or bandwidth was tuned after inspecting outcomes as subject to specification search, and prefer studies that document outcome-blind selection.
quote: choosing the window without looking at the outcome results minimizes pre-testing and specification-searching issues

title: Four falsification tests: covariates, density, placebo cutoffs, window sensitivity
guidance: Validation evidence for the regression discontinuity assumptions comes from four analyses: null effects on predetermined covariates and placebo outcomes, a density or binomial test for sorting at the cutoff, no effects at artificial cutoffs, and robustness to the neighbourhood choice. All predetermined covariates and placebo outcomes should be analysed with the same window, inference procedure and test statistic as the main outcome.
action: Code each regression discontinuity study for which of the four falsification analyses are reported and whether they used the same specification as the main analysis.
quote: An important principle behind this type of falsification analysis is that all predetermined covariates and placebo outcomes should be analyzed in the same way as the outcome of interest.

title: Window sensitivity analysis should only shrink the window
guidance: If the window was chosen as the largest with covariate balance, results in larger windows are unreliable because treated and control groups become imbalanced on important covariates. Sensitivity checks should therefore use only smaller windows, which in practice is limited by the few observations near the cutoff.
action: Do not credit robustness checks that expand a balance-selected window; look for results in smaller windows instead.
quote: results in windows larger than W0 will not be reliable because in such windows the treated and control groups will be imbalanced in important covariates

title: Fuzzy designs need exclusion and monotonicity to recover complier effects
guidance: With imperfect compliance, the intention-to-treat and first-stage effects are identified under extended continuity or local randomization assumptions, but interpreting their ratio as a treatment effect requires that assignment affects outcomes only through treatment received and that there are no defiers near the cutoff. Under monotonicity the fuzzy parameter is the average effect at the cutoff for compliers, not for all units.
action: For fuzzy regression discontinuity studies, check that the paper reports intention-to-treat and first-stage effects separately and argues the no-defier condition before interpreting the ratio.
quote: under the additional assumption of monotonicity, the Fuzzy RD parameters recover the average effect of the treatment at the cutoff for compliers

title: Falsify fuzzy designs on assignment, not on treatment received
guidance: In a fuzzy regression discontinuity, validation tests (covariate balance, density, placebo cutoffs) should be based on the assignment rule at the cutoff, exactly as in a sharp design, because it is assignment that is as-if random; treatment received is a choice that can be confounded with potential outcomes. The authors also note that weak first stages raise weak-instrument concerns.
action: Reject fuzzy regression discontinuity falsification analyses that compare treated and untreated units by treatment received rather than by position relative to the cutoff.
quote: in a Fuzzy RD design, the main falsification analyses should be implemented based on the treatment assignment and not on the treatment received

title: With discrete scores, effective sample size equals mass points
guidance: When many units share score values, local polynomial methods behave as if each mass point were one observation, so a dataset of tens of thousands of students may effectively contain only a few hundred points. Continuity-based analysis is defensible only when mass points are numerous and dense near the cutoff; otherwise extrapolation from the nearest mass points is unavoidable and local randomization is the natural alternative.
action: For each regression discontinuity study with a discrete score, record the number of distinct score values near the cutoff and treat the raw sample size as uninformative about precision.
quote: Local polynomial methods will behave essentially as if each mass point is a single observation

title: Discrete scores force parametric extrapolation to the cutoff
guidance: Because no observations lie arbitrarily close to the cutoff, the canonical effect at the cutoff cannot be nonparametrically point identified from a discrete score no matter how large the sample; retaining that parameter requires parametric extrapolation from the closest mass points, while local randomization or a redefined parameter avoids the extrapolation at the cost of a different estimand.
action: Where a study with a discrete running variable reports a continuity-based estimate, record the extrapolation assumption it relies on as part of the design's assumptions.
quote: extrapolation via additional parametric assumptions from the closest mass points above and below the cutoff to the cutoff point will be needed, no matter how large the sample size is

title: Pooled multi-cutoff effects are weighted averages dominated by dense cutoffs
guidance: Normalising scores and pooling across cutoffs yields a single effect that equals a weighted average of cutoff-specific effects, with weights proportional to the number of observations near each cutoff. The pooled parameter hides heterogeneity across cutoffs or along a geographic boundary, so it should be complemented with cutoff- or location-specific estimates.
action: When a regression discontinuity study pools multiple cutoffs or boundary points, note which cutoffs dominate the weighted average and whether cutoff-specific effects are also reported.
quote: these pooled treatment effects are equal to a weighted average of the corresponding cutoff-specific RD treatment effects

title: Extrapolating across cutoffs needs a parallel-trends-like assumption
guidance: Multiple cutoffs allow learning about effects away from a cutoff by using the control group facing a higher cutoff, but only under an assumption that pre-existing differences between the two subpopulations are constant across score values, analogous to parallel trends in difference-in-differences. Assuming the two populations are identical is valid only if cutoffs were randomly assigned.
action: Flag any regression discontinuity extrapolation claim and record the cross-subpopulation assumption (constant bias or random cutoff assignment) it depends on.
quote: An alternative assumption is that any pre-existing differences between the two subpopulations are constant for all values of the score.
